newsitem.title: USA: Amtrak employee kills one, wounds two fellow workers. [CORRECTED 22:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Amtrak employee kills one, wounds two fellow workers. [CORRECTED 22:55 GMT]

text.p: An Amtrak machinist killed a foreman and critically wounded two fellow employees in a locomotive repair shop before being shot dead himself by police on Thursday.
(Corrects headline and first paragraph to read that one person was killed and two wounded, not three killed.)

The shootings took place at the diesel maintenance building in Wilmington. The gunman, Richard D. Herr, 40, of Rehoboth Beach, Del., has been an Amtrak machinist since 1976. No reason for the shootings has been given.

Shop foreman John M. Jenson, 41, was declared dead at the scene. The other victims, John Fedora, 38, of Secaine, Penn., a general foreman, and John Morrison Jr, 34, of Newark, Del., an electrician, are listed in critical condition at the Christiana Medical Centre, a hospital spokesman said.

Acting chief Michael Boykin of the Wilmington Police Department said that when patrolman Michael Lawson and Sgt. John Randolph arrived at the diesel maintenance shop on the outskirts of Wilmington they heard shots and saw employees running from the building.

Herr, on a second story catwalk 25 feet above the ground, "confronted the police with a gun" but did not shoot. Lawson, an eight-year-veteran, shot Herr with a Remington 12 gauge shotgun, toppling him from the catwalk to the shop floor.
Boykin said Herr, who fired 15 rounds, had reloaded a 9mm handgun and also possessed a 38mm handgun.
Amtrak trains will not be affected by the incident.
